newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees emergency aid for Credit Lyonnais.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees emergency aid for Credit Lyonnais.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had approved emergency aid totalling 3.9 billion French francs ($765.6 million) for embattled French bank Credit Lyonnais.
It said in a statement that the aid was approved for 1996.
There were no other details immediately available.
Credit Lyonnais, once the largest bank outside of Japan, is being restructured under the 1995 plan allowing for a maximum of 45 billion French francs in subsidies.
It has become clear, however, that a new plan will have to be drafted if the bank is to avoid slipping again into the red.
EU sources said earlier that the Commission, which monitors state aid issues to ensure fair competition, would approve the emergency money.
But Commission officials have said the European Union executive is not happy about reports of a new French restructuring proposal. ($= 5.094 FrF)
